title: Let's talk about 'political violence'
content:
Since Charlie Kirk was shot on Wednesday, political leaders and liberal pundits have all come out of the woodwork to condemn "political violence."

"The murder of Charlie Kirk is part of a disturbing rise in political violence that threatens to hollow out our public life," Bernie Sanders said on Thursday. "Political violence has absolutely no place in our nation," Nancy Pelosi said. "Political violence is completely incompatible with American values," Hakeem Jeffries posted. "Political violence has no place in America," Kamala Harris echoed.

But the sad reality is that America was built by violence and runs on violence. Everything from the land our country occupies to the wealth that we hoard has been secured through violence. We are a country notorious for mass incarceration, police killings, and endless foreign wars. As countless people on X have pointed out, political violence is America's default setting.

When political leaders and the media wring their hands about “political violence,” they’re not actually talking about violence in any universal sense. They’re usually only talking about violence against elites or people who maintain existing power structures.

The violence that is already a daily feature of life for poor, Black, immigrant, disabled, and queer communities is invisible to them. This double standard has always been there, and it's why so many people, especially in countries that we've inflicted horrific levels of violence upon abroad, hate the American government. But cell phones and social media have finally made this hypocrisy crystal clear to more and more average Americans. The reality is that political violence has escalated over the past five years, but not in the way politicians are characterizing it.

When the pandemic started in 2020, violence against marginalized people accelerated. Immigrants, people of color, and the poor were (and are still!) being sent into deadly workplaces with no airborne disease protections. Prisoners, nursing home residents, and hospital patients are still being left to die of COVID in facilities with zero airborne disease mitigations.

When Joe Biden took office, rather than mitigate the violence of an ongoing pandemic, he forced people back to work and gave COVID funding to the police. He successfully convinced liberals (and even leftists!) to completely devalue the lives of people around them. The government got the American public to dehumanize each other so successfully that many people today believe that it's morally neutral to infect and kill, or permanently maim, those around them by spreading airborne disease because they don’t like wearing a mask. Killing and disabling millions of Americans by furthering the spread of an airborne vascular disease is also violence. The ongoing pandemic is violence.

After George Floyd was brutally murdered in 2020, millions of people took to the streets to demand an end to racist police killings. What they were met with, was an unprecedented wave of state-sanctioned violence.

The Department of Homeland Security deployed tactical teams into cities. Police kettled, beat, and arrested journalists. Protesters were shot point blank with “less-lethal” munitions, losing eyes and sustaining permanent injuries. People died in protest-related incidents. Yet none of those deaths were mourned by the mainstream media as martyrs of democracy.

After the peak of the Black Lives Matter protests, on January 6, 2021, after a violent mob stormed the capital calling for the lynching of elected officials, their violence was excused. Those rioters overwhelmingly received lighter sentences than the BLM protesters. Some used the event to launch their influencer career. Kyle Rittenhouse was acquitted of all charges for shooting anti fascist protesters dead, while peaceful college students ended up in jail.

In Atlanta in 2023, when activists protesting “Cop City” were stalked, arrested, and even killed, these pundits mourning political violence were nowhere to be seen. Manuel Terán was shot and killed and the state labeled them a “domestic terrorist” for peacefully resisting a police project. According to Mapping Police Violence, more than 1,000 people are shot and killed by police every year, overwhelmingly people of color.

When ICE raids rip apart families in the middle of the night, that is also political violence. Since January 1, 2017, at least 70 people have died in ICE custody. ICE detention facilities recorded 13 more deaths just in the first half of this year alone. These figures are likely an understatement as ICE will release people shortly before their death so they're not counted as dying under ICE custody. Just last month, a man fleeing an ICE raid at Home Depot here in Los Angeles was killed. The ACLU found that 95% of people's deaths under ICE detention were preventable.

And then of course we have school shootings, which are completely normalized. Almost the exact same time that Charlie Kirk was shot, students at Evergreen High school in Colorado were running for their lives from another school shooter.

Kirk said that victims of gun violence were necessary casualties to defend the second amendment. But we've had dozens of school shootings over the past couple decades resulting in hundreds of casualties and kids wounded. Just last year, the The American Academy of Pediatrics issued a report saying that school shootings were at an all time high and becoming even more deadly.

Americans are already exposed to unfathomable levels of political violence every day, and so the hand wringing from people in power when someone like Charlie Kirk falls victim to that same violence, rings hollow.

It especially rings hollow when our country is in the midst of facilitating a genocide. As one Palestinian posted in the wake of Charlie's death, "Sorry if I don’t seem overly shocked. It’s just I've seen decapitated babies, shredded limbs, mangled and charred bodies and much worse in Gaza for 23 months."

I think the American public being confronted with the most graphic and horrific war crimes imaginable in Palestine, has finally allowed many to see exactly how violent and hypocritical the U.S. empire is and how cavalier people in power are about that hypocrisy. (This is of course why the government wants to ban cell phones and social media, but that's a topic for another day).

As a social scientist on Twitter put it, "Political violence is never acceptable, says fascist country dominated by political state violence at every level, against every oppressed group, both within the country and around the world."

Another Muslim woman tweeted, "Political violence is being condemned across the U.S. after Charlie Kirk’s death. Where is that outrage when 100+ Palestinians are being killed with American weapons every single day?"

All these mealy mouthed statements from politicians do is reveal whose lives matter to them and whose lives don't. The daily political violence that millions of Americans have to endure through incarceration, medical neglect, deportation, police brutality, and on and on, doesn’t count. Palestinian children shot in the neck are never nationally mourned, students shot in the neck by school shooters aren't nationally mourned. But a right wing political commentator, who defended those people's deaths, is treated as a national hero.

Kirk dedicated his life to upholding these violent systems and advocated for incredibly violent policies that have resulted in people's deaths. His legions of supporters still support that violence. Before his body was even cold, far right figures were calling for a war on trans people. Many are the same people who relentlessly celebrated the killing of George Floyd and mocked the suicide of a trans girl.

Elon Musk posted to his 225 million followers, “The Left is the party of murder.” Right wing activist Laura Loomer, who has been celebrating the slaughter of Palestinian children for months, called on Trump to “shut down, defund, & prosecute every single Leftist organization,” adding that “The Left is a national security threat.” Loomer said that “More people will be murdered if the Left isn’t crushed with the power of the state."

Trump blamed the shooting on “radical left political violence” in an Oval Office address. Sean Davis, the CEO and co-founder of the Federalist, posted on X: “I hope that Trump also orders the extermination of the entire anarcho-terrorist network that has been terrorizing Christians in this nation unabated for more than a decade.”

As someone who is actually against violence, all of this is terrifying.

As many have pointed out, the whole "this shooting is going to be used as a pretense to strip us all of our rights" thing rings a little hollow when the government is already stripping us all of our rights. They certainly don't need Kirk's death to continue to brutally oppress and murder minorities with state sanctioned violence.

But it is disturbing how many self-professed liberals are already manufacturing consent for this to happen. Several high profile liberal influencers and media figures are already white washing Kirk's legacy and policy positions, framing him as an innocent father who, while they might have had some disagreements with, was fundamentally a good man.

Ezra Klein declared that while he and Charlie have had their differences, ultimately, they were "on the same side." The Yankees flew their flags at half mast as did a slew of government buildings. Liberal influencers posted teary eulogies to TikTok. CBS News, ABC, CNN, POLITICO, and dozens more news outlets ran breathless stories about the sharp escalation of "political violence" in America.

As my friend Matt Bernstein said, "Charlie Kirk's death can't be separated from the very systems he devoted his career to promoting." What we need is to dismantle those violent systems, and we can't do that when people in power still refuse to acknowledge them.

Covid, Gaza, and all the events of the past few years have revealed just how many people's lives are truly expendable. We see people in the highest positions of power in this country pushing the idea that poor, disabled, unhoused, and trans people are better off dead.

A few months ago I made a video called "someone's needs to do it" about the popular meme encouraging someone to finally assassinate Trump. In that video, I talked about how asking the public to uphold norms while almost no one in government or in power holds themselves to the same standards is a farce. I cited a research report that found that more and more Americans endorsed direct political violence and are expressing a plummeting faith in our political system and democracy. All of this is extremely concerning.

Josh Citarella, a researcher who studies extremism, told me that "the liberal project has basically failed. The enormous accumulation of wealth and power [by oligarchs] invalidates the rules of law. The end result is that you can theoretically have executions in the Public Square. That is what we're going back to."

I don't think most of us want to live in a country where political violence is the norm. I don't think most people want to feel like the only way they can fight back against oppression is through extra judicial killings. That's a really dangerous and terrible system for everyone involved that I very much do not support. I can’t stress that enough.

But we need to start demanding accountability from leaders who condemn political violence while continuing to support violent systems. Political violence is not something that we are “sliding towards," unfortunately, it's something that we are marinating in as Americans every day. We need to force people in power to acknowledge that reality if we ever want change.

  • Political analyst Matthew Dowd has been fired from MSNBC after the most benign comments ever about the death of Charlie Kirk.
